comments.author: dick_shane_e
comments.body:
For pixel art, there tends to be very technical, specific guidelines, such as consistent pixel density, clean pixel clusters, avoiding zigzags or incoherent jiggles which AI tends to do with pixel art, selective palette as someone else mentioned, perspective consistency, etc.

For a model to get all those things right, it needs more training than just a drawing. It needs to understand the theory behind pixel art, which models usually do not put into practice (not sure if it's possible to train them to be strict about this, but I feel like theoretically it should be possible).

replies.author: Hot-Spare5735
replies.body:
I would say one big issue is your background is at a very low resolution.  You are going to want the pixels on your character to be the same size as the pixels on the background.  If you tried that now, your characters would be very blocky.  You'll want your background to be higher resolution than it is now.  
  
This video gives a good into various pixel resolutions for screens for systems over the years.

[What Size is Pixel Art? (Intro to Sprite and Canvas Size)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ad-3dn2qUUs)

These resolutions fit perfectly in 1920 x 1080 resolution. (Included similar retro console)

160 x 90 (1/12) - GB  
192 x 108 (1/10) - Atari 2600  
320 x 180 (1/6) - GBA  
384 x 216 (1/5) - NES/SNES/Genesis  
480 x 270 (1/4) - Hyperlight Drifter

Someone also posted a PixelArt cleanup tool they made for Free that you could use to improve your pixel art once you have it how you want it.

[PixelAid | Oscar Sanchez](https://oscarsanchez.com/tools/pixelaid/)

To understand the theory behind something, and not just parrot it back to us, it does indeed need consciousness/intelligence. Trouble is till we get something that actually classifies as AI, and isn't just an imitation of it, then it'll never actually understand what it's doing. Problem with art is the thing that makes it good, is creativity. You may be able to devise a good algorithm to generate art with LLMs, but it's always going to be lacking without the intelligence component. 


Reddit though will downvote me for this because they don't actually understand how AI works, or what constitutes as intelligence.

comments.author: theMikaro

https://i.redd.it/h3ccc9fnoj2h1.gif

Generating actually good pixel art with AI is way harder than most people think. I’m building around this problem, and getting clean, consistent results is still a huge challenge.

One thing that helped a lot is adding a pixel-perfect grid cutting system directly into the app, so outputs snap properly into real pixel art instead of looking blurry or messy.

Still experimenting and improving it every day. if anyone here is also working on AI pixel art, I’d love to hear what workflows or tools gave you the best results.

comments.author: FreeEye5
comments.body:
This looks like fairly generic stuff, like, I've seen that dragon a thousand times. Maybe you got lucky that the style you're going for is heavily represented in training data.

The thing is, the pipeline if diffusion based image generation to pixel art is all backward. Models generate highly detailed images that get filtered down and transformed to resemble pixel art, and it always ends up looking a bit like a fuzzy approximation. 

I've been messing with tools that let language models draw on a canvas pixel by pixel, but that goes too far in the other direction for what you're after - Claude code is bad at drawing.
